title: SourceCodester Class and Exam Timetabling System 1.0 — Reflected XSS via 'day' parameter

exposure.note: Self-hosted PHP/Apache app (typically XAMPP). Reachable on whatever HTTP(S) port the site is served on.

affected_technologies.note: No official patch exists for V1.0.

preconditions: No authentication required — the vulnerable admin pages echo the parameter before any access check on the reflection path.

log_monitoring_urls.reason: Echoes 'day' into HTML with no output encoding.
Echoes 'day' into HTML with no output encoding.

request_signatures: day= value containing HTML/JS injection: <script, %3Cscript, </script>, <svg, <img, onerror=, onload=, javascript:
behavioral: Referer or victim requests to /admin/class.php or /admin/BSIS.php with a scripted 'day' value delivered via a crafted link (email/chat) — reflected XSS requires victim interaction.
Outbound callbacks (data exfiltration / session theft) to attacker domains immediately following a reflected payload hit.

remediation.primary: No official patch exists. Apply context-aware output encoding to the 'day' parameter and validate against an allow-list of weekday values.
steps: Encode on output: echo htmlspecialchars($day, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'); at every sink that renders 'day'.
Validate on input: reject any 'day' value not in {Monday..Sunday} (or the app's expected day set) before use.
Add a Content-Security-Policy (e.g. default-src 'self'; script-src 'self') to blunt reflected-XSS impact.
mitigations_if_upgrade_impossible: Deploy the WAF virtual patch below.
Restrict /admin/ to trusted source IPs / behind authentication at the reverse proxy.

signatures.description: HTML tag injection in the 'day' parameter.
Inline event handler or javascript: URI in 'day'.
Preferred rule: block any 'day' value that is not a plain weekday name.

waf.combine: block if any negative signature matches, or (preferred) if the allow-list rule fails
waf.false_positive_notes: 'day' is expected to be a weekday name; the positive allow-list is the most robust and lowest-false-positive rule.
